subject.title: [Feature]: Optional session activity watchdog and alerts (blocked by #39127)

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in session activity watchdog and operator alerting surface after the sessions.activity API lands, or should core expose activity/diagnostic signals for plugins and dashboards to consume?
rationale: The request adds new core feature, config, delivery, privacy, UI/operator, and optional model-call behavior rather than repairing an existing contract, so automation cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Keep as downstream core design item
options.body: Keep this issue open until the canonical sessions.activity contract lands, then design a default-off core watchdog around that single source of session truth.

options.title: Route alerting to plugins
options.body: Have core expose activity and diagnostics only, with alert delivery, webhooks, and tokenized summaries owned by plugins or dashboards.

options.title: Defer watchdog scope
options.body: Leave this parked until real operator incidents clarify the minimum alerting surface beyond diagnostics and UI status.

recommendation.title: Keep as downstream core design item
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until the canonical sessions.activity contract lands, then design a default-off core watchdog around that single source of session truth.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the strongest current gateway/session code-history routing candidate from the checked-out sessions and diagnostic surfaces.
